To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parental BMI was associated, after accounting for offspring lifestyle factors, with offspring BMI, and with offspring CVD risk factors in mid-life.
parental obesity is associated with adverse risk factors for cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) in mid-life offspring.
parental obesity and offspring obesity are both associated with increased risk factors for CDS, and these associations may be mediated through adiposity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the intergenerational influences on health.
the intergenerational transmission of obesity and its effects on health.
the association of parental adiposity with offspring cardiovascular health in mid-life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parental adiposity was not associated with CVD risk among their offspring in this cohort.
parental obesity is associated with increased CVD risk in their offspring, which is largely mediated by offspring obesity.
there are associations between higher parental BMI and less favourable offspring levels of CVD risk factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parental adiposity is related to less favourable CVD risk profiles in their offspring, and that these associations are largely mediated by offspring adiposity.
parental BMI is not associated with offspring CVD risk, but that the association of offspring BMI with some CVD risk markers is modified by parental BMI.

parental BMI is associated with offspring BMI and that both of these factors are associated with CVD risk in mid-life, although the associations between BMI and CVD risk are mediated by adiposity and the associations between BMI in the parents and CVD risk among the offspring are mediated by BMI in the offspring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the offspring’s adiposity mediates much, if not all, of the effect of parental BMI on CVD-related risk factors.
offspring BMI was a stronger predictor of CVD risk than parental BMI.
the association between BMI and risk factors is stronger among offspring whose parents were heavier.
